learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems within their area of study.
Ability of abstraction: ability to create and use models that reflect real situations.

Ability for effective oral and written communication (in expression and comprehension), with special emphasis on technical documentation writing.
Possess the necessary learning skills to undertake further studies or improve their training with a certain degree of autonomy.
Be motivated by quality and continuous improvement and act rigorously in professional development.

assessment_rules: For ordinary assessment, the final grade is calculated as NOTA FINAL = EX.ORD + P1 + P2 + P3 + P. A minimum of 40% (2.6 points) is required in the final theoretical-practical exam (EX.ORD), which has a maximum score of 6.5 points. A minimum of 40% (1.4 points) is required in the sum of the three evaluable practices (P1, P2, P3) and participation (P), which together have a maximum score of 3.5 points. To pass, a final grade of at least 5 points is needed, with all minimums met. If minimums are met but the final grade is below 5, the student fails with the obtained grade; if the final grade is above 5 but a minimum is not met, the final grade is 4.5. Extraordinary assessment involves a theoretical-practical exam (EX.EXTR) and/or a practical exam (EX.PR), with similar minimums and grading rules based on which components are retaken.
